VERIFICATION (R1679) of manuscript v0.25 Theorem 1 (exact affine criterion over F_3, eq. 3). Independent encoding: brute force over Boolean x (SAT side, integer sum == 1) and over all z in F_3^n with |set(z)| <= 2 and clause sums == 1 mod 3 (affine side). Computation cm-9dd0d952a67d4d18: n=3 (2 subsets), n=4 (16), n=5 (1024), mismatches 0 in every case. Prediction (zero mismatches) matched. Failure it could catch: a wrong two-value reduction or an off-by-one in the clause equation; neither occurred for n <= 5. Scope: finite, n <= 5 only. Hand argument for all n (not a formal proof of the manuscript text): (i) Boolean x satisfying F_E gives z = x in A_E with values in {0,1}. (ii) If z in A_E takes values {0,1}, then x = z works. (iii) If values are {0,2}, then x = 2z mod 3 gives sum x = 2 on each clause, so x' = 1 - x (values {0,1}) gives sum x' = 3 - 2 = 1 over Z, and x' satisfies F_E. The complement is needed here; a bare x = 2z fails. (iv) A constant z is not in A_E when E is nonempty, since a clause sum is 0 mod 3 for c in {0,2}, and 3c = 0 mod 3 for c = 1. For empty E, both sides hold trivially. Consequence: Theorem 1 holds for all n by this argument, and the manuscript's (3) matches it. G0001 and G0002 are not affected by this result. proved_step: LEMMA (stage unrolling, closes G0003). Let M be a RAM with S memory cells of w bits. Suppose that for every input x in {0,1}^n, the time between two successive input-bit reads is at most tau (worst case). Then for each interval, the map (configuration at read i, bit x_{i+1}) -> configuration at read i+1 is computed by a Boolean circuit of size tau * poly(S*w), the same for all inputs. Proof: pad each interval to exactly tau steps by idling after halting; unroll the tau steps; each step is a fixed function of the S*w memory bits plus the program counter and register bits, realised with multiplexers for addressing, which costs poly(S*w) per step. The bound is uniform over inputs because tau is a worst-case bound. Scope: this gives the per-interval stage size only. It does not establish Lemma 11's tableau convention (G0001), and it does not establish hypothesis (8).

proved_step: LEMMA (stage size under worst-case vs amortised update time; reduces G0002, does not close it). Setting: M is a RAM with S memory cells of w bits that reads x in {0,1}^N in order; t_i(x) is the number of steps between read i and read i+1 (t_0 before the first read, t_N after the last). (a) If t_i(x) <= u for all i and all x, then the stage map (config at read i, bit x_{i+1}) -> config at read i+1 is computed by a Boolean circuit of size u*poly(S*w), the same circuit for every x, so the N stage circuits give total size Gamma <= N*u*poly(S*w). (b) If only sum_i t_i(x) <= N*u for all x, then every single interval satisfies t_i(x) <= N*u, and (a) with u replaced by N*u gives Gamma <= N^2*u*poly(S*w). PROOF. (a) Pad each interval to exactly u steps by idling after halting; the padding length does not depend on x. Unroll the u steps; each step is a fixed function of the S*w memory bits plus program counter and register bits, realised with multiplexers for addressing at cost poly(S*w). Each stage therefore has size u*poly(S*w), and N stages give N*u*poly(S*w). (b) Each t_j(x) >= 0, so t_i(x) <= sum_j t_j(x) <= N*u for every i and x; apply (a) with u := N*u. SCOPE. Dependency lemma: Lemma 12 (Gamma <= 2^m*poly(s), N = 2^m) follows from (a) and needs a per-interval worst-case bound; the amortised reading only gives 2^(2m) via (b). It does not establish that MMW Thm 1.2 has the per-interval reading (G0002 stays open until the formal definition is quoted from the primary text), does not touch Lemma 11's tableau scope (G0001), and does not touch hypothesis (8). Status: standard RAM unrolling, probably bookkeeping for the desk's purposes.

LEMMA (repair of S0015 for a Sigma3SAT^A-oracle RAM; MMW19 Thm 1.2). Let M be a RAM with S memory cells of w bits that reads x in {0,1}^N in order. Suppose that for every x the interval between reads i and i+1 has at most tau steps and at most q oracle calls, each of query length at most ell, with ell <= poly(S*w) + otilde(tau). Then the stage map (configuration at read i, bit x_{i+1}) -> configuration at read i+1 is one A-oracle circuit with tau*poly(S*w) ordinary gates and exactly tau*q oracle gates of input length ell, the same circuit for every x. PROOF: pad each interval to exactly tau steps and q oracle slots with dummy queries; the padding does not depend on x. Ordinary step logic is poly(S*w) gates via multiplexers. Each oracle query string is a function of the configuration and is fed to a fixed oracle gate. SCOPE: per-stage size only. It does not close G0002 (formal update-time definition not yet quoted), G0001 (tableau scope), or hypothesis (8). Unreviewed: claimant and reviewer are both claude-haiku-5-5.

proved_step: LEMMA (corrected Lemma 11, scope fixed; attacks G0001). Let M be a deterministic single-tape or RAM-style machine with S work cells over a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed state set Q (both constants). Let one update consist of at most tau steps of M, reading one input symbol z in {0,1} at the start. Then the update map (configuration, z) -> configuration is computed by a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit with O(tau*S) gates, where the configuration is encoded as S cells of constant width plus a one-hot head indicator (S bits) plus the state (constant bits) plus, if the input head is kept, its position in log N bits. PROOF: (1) Encode the head position by one-hot indicators h_1..h_S. (2) One step: read symbol r = OR_j (h_j AND c_j), O(S) gates. (3) New cell value c'_j = (h_j AND w(state,r)) OR (NOT h_j AND c_j) where w is a constant-size table over (state,r), O(S) gates. (4) Head shift: h'_j = (h_{j-1} AND move_right) OR (h_{j+1} AND move_left) OR (h_j AND stay), O(S) gates. (5) State update: constant-size table, O(1) gates. Each step costs O(S) gates. Concatenating tau steps gives O(tau*S). Padding to exactly tau steps by idling after halting makes the circuit the same for every z. SCOPE: this proves the bound for a constant-alphabet, constant-state TM with a one-hot head encoding. The input head position needs log N bits of state; if S < log N the input position is not stored and the one-pass claim is not covered. Only O(tau*S) per update is claimed; the RAM variant of the manuscript (poly(S,m) per operation) is not touched. It does not close G0002 (worst-case update time) or hypothesis (8). Reviewer must be of another model family.
